title: Decisions With More Than One Condition
content:
What problem does this solve?
Clearance for the abandoned route once used by Captain Ilyra Venn depends on supplies, a guide, and active warnings. Real decisions often ask whether several conditions are true together—or whether any one danger is enough to stop the plan.

Previously in your program
Your intake desk already classifies supplies with if / elif / else: Cleared for 10+, Review for 5–9, Denied below 5. If supplies is 7, the Review branch runs because 7 fails >= 10 and then matches >= 5.

Basic syntax
  if has_guide and supplies >= 10 and not storm_warning:
      print("Departure approved")
  else:
      print("Hold at camp")

What actually happens
Boolean expressions evaluate to True or False. and requires both sides true. or requires at least one side true. not reverses a Boolean value. Parentheses make grouping clear when and and or appear together.

When this is useful
Translate the English rule first, then choose and, or, and not to match it.
concepts: and is true only when every part is true
or is true when at least one part is true
Parentheses make mixed and/or rules readable

examples.title: Departure rule
examples.code:
has_guide = True
supplies = 11
storm_warning = False

if has_guide and supplies >= 10 and not storm_warning:
    print("Departure approved")
else:
    print("Hold at camp")
examples.explanation: All three requirements pass, so Departure approved prints.

common_mistakes: Replacing and with or because both words feel interchangeable
Writing if supplies >= 10 and <= 20: without repeating the variable
Confusing Boolean True/False with the strings "True" and "False"
Forgetting parentheses when mixing and and or

exercises.title: The warning flag
exercises.prompt: What does this print? Evaluate each part of the condition, including not.
exercises.code_to_predict:
has_guide = True
supplies = 12
warning_active = True

if has_guide and supplies >= 10 and not warning_active:
    print("Depart")
else:
    print("Wait")
exercises.failure_message: Evaluate each part separately, including what not does to warning_active.
hints: has_guide is True and supplies >= 10 is True — what about the warning?
not warning_active flips True to False.
and needs every part true, so the else path runs and prints Wait.

exercises.title: and or or?
exercises.prompt: Any one of these should trigger a route warning: flooding is reported, the bridge is broken, or visibility is poor. Which operator belongs between the conditions?
exercises.success_message: Right. A single danger is enough, so at least one condition must be true.
exercises.failure_message: Think about whether every danger must be present, or whether one danger alone should warn the party.
hints: The English rule says any one of the dangers is enough.
and would require every listed danger at once.
Choose or so one true condition triggers the warning.

exercises.title: The false clearance
exercises.prompt: Both a guide and at least 10 supplies are required. The current code clears an expedition with no guide. Change only the Boolean operator so can_depart returns the correct result for every case.
exercises.starter_code:
def can_depart(has_guide, supplies):
    return has_guide or supplies >= 10
hints: Both requirements must pass together — one alone is not enough.
or is true when either side is true; that clears a guide-less party with enough supplies.
Replace or with and so both the guide and the supply check must succeed.

tests.message: Inside can_depart, combine the requirements with and (not or).

exercises.title: Departure clearance
exercises.prompt: Write can_depart(has_guide, supplies, warning_active). Return True only when there is a guide, supplies are at least 10, and no warning is active. Otherwise return False.
hints: All three safety requirements must pass together.
Use and between the requirements. The warning requirement needs to be reversed.
Combine has_guide, supplies >= 10, and not warning_active.

tests.message: Inside can_depart, combine the safety requirements with and.
Inside can_depart, use not so an active warning blocks departure.

exercises.title: Either route is usable
exercises.prompt: Write has_escape_route(north_open, south_open) that returns True if either route is open.
hints: Either route being open is enough.
The operator for "at least one" is or.

tests.message: Inside has_escape_route, combine the routes with or.
